summary: Former Kern County tower on Cook Peak in Sequoia NF: 25-foot steel tower by 1942, staffed into the 1950s, abandoned in a 1968 fire; 2005 photos show foundation blocks only.

facts.status_note: Listed as Gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; 2005 photos show only concrete foundation blocks
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sequoia National Forest

events.note: Telephone line being built to Cook Peak; a new lookout was to be built in the near future
Fire burned 12,000 acres the first night and encircled the lookout; tower and house undamaged
Cliff Harrington and Robert Crain manned the lookout during the fire
Claude Stewart said he had been a lookout on the peak for four years
Mrs. Helen King was the Forest Service lookout on Cook's Peak
Grass and scrub oak fire near Lake Isabella moved up Cook's Peak; press reports say a small cabin, a boat and some sheds burned in the same fire
Lookout station abandoned during the fire

notes_for_editor: Build year is not given: a 1936 item says a new lookout was to be built, and a 1942 item describes a tower and house. The 1968 sentence about a cabin, boat and sheds does not place them at the lookout, so the story says press reports and leaves the location open. Elevation differs: 5,200 ft in the 1947 item versus 5409 ft on Peakbagging. The index has no registry number. Sources are a compiled clippings page, an index row and a 2005 photo page.
